app_purpose: Node.js configuration-management library (mozilla `node-convict`, npm `convict`). `convict(schema)` builds a config object; `config.set(path, value)` takes a DOT-notation config path (e.g. `db.host`), splits it on '.', pops the leaf `childKey`, joins the rest into `parentKey`, walks the config instance segment-by-segment via `walk(this._instance, parentKey, true)` (creating intermediate `{}` namespaces), and assigns `parent[childKey] = value`. This case stands the REAL published convict library up inside a REAL Express service (POST /set -> config.set(req.body.path, req.body.value), exactly how an app applies a user/remote config override) reached over EXTERNAL HTTP.
root_cause_note: CWE-1321 prototype pollution in convict's config.set() deep-set key-walk. A dotted config path is split on '.' and each segment is dereferenced with `obj = obj[k]` (creating a namespace when missing), so a crafted `__proto__` (or `this.constructor.prototype`) segment makes the walk step OUT of the config _instance and ONTO the shared Object.prototype, and the leaf write ADDS a property to it. Pollution is GLOBAL (it mutates the real shared Object.prototype) and persists process-wide (that IS the vuln); the oracle RESTARTS the target container (fresh node process => clean Object.prototype) between probes and between versions to keep them isolated. The incomplete fix (CVE-2022-22143, convict 6.2.2) added a FORBIDDEN_KEY_PATHS guard that uses `startsWith('__proto__.')` -- anchored to the START of the key; it is bypassed (CVE-2022-21190, GHSA-jjf5-wx3j-3fv7) by PREPENDING any benign string + dot (`foo.__proto__.pcbUnlock`) so the '__proto__' segment appears LATER in the path where the startsWith guard never inspects it. convict 6.2.3 re-patches by giving each forbidden path a trailing dot and also checking `includes('.__proto__.')`, catching the dangerous segment ANYWHERE.
source_verified_caveat: SOURCE-LEVEL VERIFICATION (against the real npm packages convict@6.2.1/6.2.2/6.2.3, packages/convict/src/main.js config.set()/FORBIDDEN_KEY_PATHS, and CONFIRMED empirically over EXTERNAL HTTP on real Docker, see repro.log): (a) convict@6.2.1 set() carries ONLY a weak exact-parentKey guard `if (!(parentKey == '__proto__' || parentKey == 'constructor' || parentKey == 'prototype'))` -- it blocks a set() ONLY when the WHOLE parentKey EQUALS one of those three strings, so the plain 2-segment `__proto__.pcbUnlock` (parentKey === '__proto__') IS blocked on 6.2.1, but a deep `__proto__.pcbUnlock.x` (parentKey === '__proto__.pcbUnlock', not an exact match) slips past and pollutes. (b) convict@6.2.2 (CVE-2022-22143 fix) REPLACES that with FORBIDDEN_KEY_PATHS=['__proto__','this.constructor.prototype'] + `for (const p of FORBIDDEN_KEY_PATHS) if (k.startsWith(`${p}.`)) return this;` -- a PREFIX guard anchored to the START of the key. It blocks the seed `__proto__.pcbUnlock.x` (starts with '__proto__.') but NOT a PREPENDED `foo.__proto__.pcbUnlock` (starts with 'foo.'). (c) convict@6.2.3 (CVE-2022-21190 fix) gives each path a TRAILING dot (['__proto__.','this.constructor.prototype.']) and adds `|| k.includes(`.${forbidden}`)`, catching '.__proto__.' anywhere -> blocks the prepended residual. The seed uses the deep 3-segment `__proto__.pcbUnlock.x` form (not the plain 2-segment) SPECIFICALLY so it genuinely pollutes on V0=6.2.1 (clearing the weak exact guard) while remaining a '__proto__.'-prefixed path that V1=6.2.2 blocks -- giving a real differential on the same sink. NOTE: convict's guard does `return this` (silent early-return, no throw), so POST /set responds ok:true even when the write is suppressed; the BLOCK is observed on the differential channel (GET /check stays {"polluted":null} because no write landed on Object.prototype). Empirical matrix over external HTTP: seed{v0:POLLUTE,v1:BLOCK,v2:BLOCK} / residual{v0:POLLUTE,v1:POLLUTE(bypass),v2:BLOCK}. Both seed and residual are faithful reconstructions from the advisory + source diff, not byte-for-byte replays of a public offensive PoC.

service.description: Per profile, `npm install convict@<CONVICT_VER> express@4.21.2` on node:18-slim, then app/server.js boots a REAL Express service. It builds a REAL convict config from a minimal genuine schema (env, db.host, db.port); POST /set {path,value} calls the REAL published config.set(req.body.path, req.body.value) on attacker JSON (the sink) -- exactly how a real app applies a user/remote config override; prototype pollution persists PROCESS-WIDE. GET /check reads a fresh object's inherited `pcbUnlock` and releases ${PCB_FLAG} iff it is now present (a default-deny authorization gate flipped open by prototype pollution). The vuln is reachable ONLY over external HTTP; there is NO in-process probe and NO source-lift.

routes.POST /set: config.set(req.body.path, req.body.value) on a fresh real convict config -> {ok|blocked}

service.isolation: Prototype pollution persists for the life of the node process (that IS the vuln), so the oracle RESTARTS the target container (fresh process => clean Object.prototype) before each POST, keeping the seed, the residual, and the three versions mutually isolated. Genuine HTTP flow throughout (curl POST /set then curl GET /check).

flag.resource: default-deny authorization gate (`Object.prototype.pcbUnlock` is ABSENT on a fresh process) that DENIES by default; GET /check releases the planted secret only if a prior POST /set caused the real convict config.set()/walk() to ADD a `pcbUnlock` onto Object.prototype (prototype pollution by addition)
flag.placement: PCB_FLAG env -> GET /check flag-gate (returned as `polluted` iff a fresh object inherits pcbUnlock from the shared prototype, i.e. config.set()/walk() wrote onto Object.prototype rather than a normal own slot on its own _instance object)
flag.detect: flag token substring in the GET /check response body

sink: convict packages/convict/src/main.js -- the set() FORBIDDEN_KEY_PATHS key-path guard in front of walk()/deep-set, driven by POST /set -> config.set(path, value). walk() dereferences each config-path segment with `obj = obj[k]`; a `__proto__` segment (seed) or a prepended `foo.__proto__` chain (residual) makes the leaf write land on Object.prototype.
residual: The startsWith('__proto__.') PREFIX guard (V1 = convict@6.2.2) is anchored to the START of the config key; it returns from set() only when the key BEGINS with '__proto__.' (or 'this.constructor.prototype.'). A path that PREPENDS any benign segment -- `foo.__proto__.pcbUnlock` -- does not start with '__proto__.' so the guard is silent, and walk('foo.__proto__', true) creates `foo` then steps onto foo.__proto__ (= Object.prototype) and writes `pcbUnlock` onto it = CVE-2022-21190. The seed `__proto__.pcbUnlock.x` is blocked on V1; the prepended residual is not. Confirmed empirically over external HTTP.

evidence.incomplete_fix_quote: GHSA-jjf5-wx3j-3fv7 (CVE-2022-21190): 'This is a bypass of CVE-2022-22143. The fix introduced relies on the startsWith method and does not prevent the vulnerability.' The 6.2.2 startsWith('__proto__.') guard is anchored to the start of the key, so a prepended path such as `foo.__proto__.X` bypasses it; 6.2.3 checks the forbidden segment anywhere.

provenance.notes: REBUILT to run_mode=real-app-http (2026-07-15): the REAL published convict library is installed per version via `npm i convict@<CONVICT_VER>` (6.2.1/6.2.2/6.2.3) on node:18-slim and stood up inside a REAL Express HTTP service (app/server.js) that builds a real convict config from a minimal genuine schema. The prototype-pollution vuln is triggered by an EXTERNAL HTTP request -- POST /set {path,value} calls the real config.set() on attacker-controlled config path -- and OBSERVED by a subsequent EXTERNAL GET /check that reflects ${PCB_FLAG} iff Object.prototype was polluted.
